speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the gait and limb ataxia you are experiencing, including when it started and whether it has been getting worse?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. You mentioned a significant medical history in your profile; could you please specify what conditions you have been diagnosed with in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and recent natalizumab use, I need to ask: have you experienced any fever, headaches, or changes in vision or speech recently? Additionally, has your ataxia progressed rapidly over days to weeks, or has it been a slow, gradual decline over months?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of natalizumab use and subacute neurological deficits like ataxia and weakness raises strong suspicion for Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). I need to visualize the brain to look for characteristic white matter lesions, so REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_with_contrast.
